reason: Stopping a turn with a required (failure_policy block) stop hook logged chat.native_hook.terminal_failure at ERROR as ChatError('required native hook ... did not complete: hook exited unsuccessfully') <- CancelledError on every stop. The hook had run; CancelledError was only the implicit __context__ because chat.turn.cancelled/failed hooks ran inside the except handlers of _produce_provider_turn and complete(), and the real cause (the hook's exit code and stderr) stayed on the NativeHookExecution row. The cancelled/failed payloads also lacked finish_reason (only completed had it), so a stop hook reading it failed on every stop; tool-enabled turns never ran chat.turn.completed hooks; and a stop while a hook ran left its execution 'running' forever because NativeHookRunner.run was cancelled at asyncio.to_thread and never wrote the outcome. Now terminal hooks run after the handlers; for failed/cancelled a block-policy failure is not raised (the turn already ended) but recorded as a WARNING chat.native_hook.terminal_hook_failed with hook_id, exit_code (new allowlisted metadata keys), execution_id and a bounded, redacted stderr excerpt; all three turn-end events carry provider_id, model, finish_reason (provider reason or stop / failed / cancelled) and detail, documented in the hook starter script; _stream_tool_turn runs chat.turn.completed once before persisting the final answer; and the runner shields the hook process and records its real outcome when it exits, leaving an execution that Core shutdown already marked interrupted for reconciliation untouched. tests/v3/test_native_hook_turn_ends.py is new: 7 of its 8 tests fail on main, the eighth (core_shutdown) guards the unchanged restart-reconciliation contract. The listed existing node ids exercise the changed runner, producer, complete() and hook starter directly.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the real-Core journey suite matched through src/nebula/v3/chat.py, native_hooks.py, diagnostics.py and guides.py) does not stop a turn during or with a failing lifecycle hook or run hooks on tool turns; the Python tests drive these paths directly. The broader chat, tool-loop, native-hook, guide, diagnostics, goal, queue, schedule, subagent, reconnection and chat API files were run locally, not in CI. No full suites.
